587	## D-025 — Backend testing strategy (async fixtures, per-test DB copies, trigger tests on SQLite)
588	
589	**Decision.**
590	pytest + pytest-asyncio with `asyncio_mode=auto`; HTTP tests use `httpx.AsyncClient` over `ASGITransport(app)` — no live server.
591	
592	**Database isolation uses the TEMPLATE-COPY pattern**, deliberately replacing the draft's SAVEPOINT/join-external-transaction approach, which breaks the moment code under test performs REAL commits — and ours does by design (idempotency's separate reservation transaction, `run_in_uow` commits, numbering claims): a session-scoped fixture builds ONE migrated template SQLite file via programmatic `alembic.command.upgrade(config, 'head')` (env.py's `asyncio.run` pattern works because the session fixture runs outside any event loop); a function-scoped fixture copies that file (`shutil.copy`, ~ms) into tmp_path, builds an aiosqlite engine on the copy with the connect-event `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`, and overrides the app's session dependency. Every test gets a fully migrated, trigger-bearing, fresh database where real commits are allowed and nothing leaks across tests. For the pg-marked subset in CI, a fixture creates a per-test database via `CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE atlas_test_template` from a once-migrated template database and drops it after — same semantics on Postgres.
593	
594	**Fixtures in `tests/conftest.py`:** `tenant_factory` provisions tenant + admin user + role with named permissions through the REAL provisioning service under `system_context`, returning a handle with tenant_id and an `auth_headers(user)` helper that performs a real login; `authed_client` composes it; `permissions_context` sets the `current_permissions` ContextVar for serializer-level masking tests; module fixtures live in `tests/modules/<module>/conftest.py` per STRUCTURE §6.
595	
596	**DB-guard tests** (`tests/modules/finance/test_journal_db_guards.py` etc.) deliberately use raw `session.execute(text(...))` to BYPASS the service layer — sanctioned because the CI grep gate banning `text()` is scoped to `app/`, not `tests/` — asserting that UPDATE/DELETE on posted lines, unbalanced DRAFT→POSTED, closed-period posting, and audit UPDATE/DELETE all raise with the `ATLAS_` tokens on SQLite, with the same tests re-run on Postgres via `-m pg`. The tenancy suite enumerates `Base.registry.mappers` (auto-covering new models); event-bus tests assert handler effects and rollback-on-handler-failure within one transaction; idempotency tests exercise the two-transaction reservation flow with real commits; determinism comes from explicit posting_date/anchor arguments in factories, not clock freezing.
597	
598	**Rationale.**
599	The template-copy pattern is the single decision that makes everything else testable as designed: SAVEPOINT isolation silently converts the idempotency guard's real COMMIT into a savepoint release (changing the very semantics under test) and shares state when code opens a second session. File copies are milliseconds on SQLite and CREATE DATABASE TEMPLATE is fast on Postgres, so the cost is negligible while every test sees the exact schema migrations produce — triggers included, which is the whole point of asserting DB guards in CI. Factories going through real services means tenancy stamping, numbering, docflow, and audit are exercised by every test that touches data.
600	
601	**Rejected alternatives.**
602	- SAVEPOINT/join-external-transaction per test (the draft): incompatible with real multi-transaction code paths and second sessions; rejected as the primary pattern.
603	- `create_all` + trigger fixture: duplicates DDL outside migrations and tests a schema nobody ships.
604	- In-memory `:memory:` SQLite: cannot be shared across connections/sessions the way the app's engine needs, and cannot be template-copied.
605	- One shared DB with truncation between tests: ordering-sensitive and slow on Postgres.
606	
607	**Risks & mitigations.**
608	- Session-scoped template means schema changes require fixture cache invalidation — the template path embeds the Alembic head revision in its filename, so a new revision automatically rebuilds.
609	- Per-test PG database creation is slower (~100 ms each) — confined to the small pg-marked subset.
610	- Raw-SQL bypass tests are tightly coupled to trigger names/tokens — intentional pinning; they exist to fail when guards change.
611	
612	---
613	
614	## D-026 — Seed-data architecture (deterministic, per-template, three months of linked transactions)
615	
616	**Decision.**
617	`backend/seed.py` is a CLI (argparse: `--templates` defaulting to all five industry templates, `--anchor-date` defaulting to today, `--reset`) that assumes a migrated database (Makefile target chains `alembic upgrade head`).
618	
619	**Determinism:** one `random.Random(f'{template}:{anchor_date}')` per tenant — identical output for a given (template, anchor) pair; the anchor is recorded on the tenant so reruns are reproducible for bug reports.
620	
621	**Provisioning phase** under `system_context()`: per template, create tenant (slug `demo-<template>`, fixed admin credentials sourced from `.env.example` values), apply the YAML industry template via the industry module's real application service — modules toggled, display labels, chart-of-accounts preset, tax codes, number-sequence patterns, system roles, custom-field defs (written through `core/custom_fields.py`).
622	
623	**Transaction phase:** set the tenancy ContextVar to the tenant (NOT `system_context` — business writes must be stamped and filtered normally) and drive everything through the REAL service layer wrapped in `run_in_uow()`, never raw inserts — so numbering, docflow registration and links, domain events (goods issue → COGS), audit rows, and DB triggers all fire exactly as in production, making seed a standing integration proof.
624	
625	**Script per template spans 3 calendar months ending at anchor:** master data first (items, vendors, customers, warehouses, employees, WBS elements, exchange rates including one foreign currency); then interlinked flows — procurement P2P chains (requisition → PO → goods receipt → AP invoice → payment run), sales O2C (quote → order → delivery → customer invoice → receipt, including partial shipments and one open backorder), template-specific depth (production orders with WIP postings for manufacturing; projects + timesheets for professional-services; maintenance orders for construction; quality inspection lots for healthcare/retail receiving), foreign-currency invoices plus a month-end FX revaluation run, manual journal entries, and month-end closes: periods for months 1 and 2 CLOSED via the real period-close service, month 3 left OPEN with open AP/AR items so aging, dunning, and dashboards have live data. Volumes ~100-300 documents per tenant (seconds on SQLite).
626	
627	**Idempotency:** without `--reset`, seed refuses if a demo tenant exists; `--reset` hard-deletes the demo tenants by cascade — the ONLY sanctioned hard-delete path in the codebase, running under `system_context` and documented as such.
628	
629	**Self-verification:** seed ends by asserting, per tenant, (a) trial balance debits == credits, (b) every created document's docflow chain traverses end-to-end, (c) inventory GL balance == sum of `inv_item_valuations` — and CI runs seed against SQLite after the test suite as a smoke gate.
630	
631	**Rationale.**
632	Seeding through real services is the load-bearing choice: SQL-dump seeds rot with every migration and bypass exactly the invariants (gapless numbers, docflow, COGS events, period triggers) the demo exists to showcase, while service-driven seeding doubles as an end-to-end integration test the CI runs for free. Deterministic RNG + recorded anchor gives reproducible demos and bug reports without freezing real time. Closing two of three months demonstrates the period-close machinery and leaves believable open items for the operational screens.
633	
634	**Rejected alternatives.**
635	- SQL dump / fixtures files: bypass invariants, drift with schema, undebuggable diffs.
636	- Faker with random seed-per-run: non-reproducible demo states.
637	- Seeding via HTTP API: needs a running server and auth choreography for zero added fidelity — the service layer is the contract.
638	- A full year of data: slower seeds for no demo value; the parity scope's reports all read well at 3 months.
639	
640	**Risks & mitigations.**
641	- Anchor defaulting to today means runs on different days differ in dates (structure stays identical given anchor) — acceptable; CI pins a fixed anchor for the smoke gate.
642	- Seed duration creeps as modules land — bounded by per-tenant volume caps and the CI timing check.
643	- The `--reset` cascade is a footgun if pointed at a non-demo tenant — guarded by a slug prefix check (refuses anything not starting with `demo-`).

1	# DECISIONS.md — Design Decision Log
2	
3	One line per consequential decision + rationale, so later sessions don't re-litigate or contradict earlier choices. Numbered, append-only; superseding a decision gets a new entry referencing the old one.
4	
5	- **D-001 Bootstrap exception to "nothing directly on main":** the `.gitignore` root commit lands directly on `main` (GITHUB-WORKFLOW.md §1 explicitly orders it first); everything else reaches `main` only via `dev` promotions. Rationale: a branch cannot be cut from an empty repo.
6	- **D-002 Python toolchain = uv + Python 3.12:** uv manages the venv, lockfile (`uv.lock`, committed) and Python pin; CI uses `astral-sh/setup-uv`. Rationale: fastest reproducible installs, single tool for venv+lock+run.
7	- **D-003 Tests on SQLite (aiosqlite), runtime on PostgreSQL:** models are written PostgreSQL-first with SQLite-compatible type fallbacks (e.g. JSON variant for JSONB, Numeric for money); the full suite and CI run against in-memory/file SQLite, while docker-compose runs Postgres. Rationale: the prompt requires PostgreSQL-first + SQLite-compatible demo; SQLite keeps CI fast and dependency-free. DB-level financial constraints must be expressed portably (CHECK constraints, not Postgres-only features) or get Postgres-only guards documented per case.
8	- **D-004 Frontend package manager = npm:** lockfile committed; no pnpm/yarn. Rationale: zero extra tooling on contributor machines.
9	- **D-005 CI check names are stable from PR #1:** single workflow `ci.yml` with jobs `backend` and `frontend`; each job no-ops green while its directory doesn't exist yet. Rationale: branch protection requires named status checks; names must exist before the code does.
10	- **D-006 Makefile and docker-compose.yml are deferred to the first backend PR:** a Makefile whose targets point at directories that don't exist would violate the no-orphan-files rule in spirit. Rationale: every committed file must work the day it lands.
11	- **D-007 Tenancy via non-bypassable session filter:** a `do_orm_execute` hook adds `with_loader_criteria(TenantMixin, ...)` reading a `current_tenant_id` ContextVar to every ORM statement (lazy loads and bulk writes included), fail-closed when unset unless `system_context()` is active (exactly four call sites); `before_flush` stamps/validates tenant_id; composite `(tenant_id, id)` FKs + SQLite `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` are the DB backstop. Only mechanism with zero cooperation from query authors. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
12	- **D-008 JWT access+refresh with CAS rotation and 10 s grace window:** HS256 with `ATLAS_JWT_SECRET`; 15-min stateless access token with `ver` checked against `core_users.token_version`; 14-day refresh JWT in an httpOnly cookie scoped to /api/v1/auth, rotated via compare-and-swap on hashed jti in `core_refresh_sessions` with reuse → family revocation, prev-jti accepted within 10 s so multi-tab races don't force logouts; argon2id (t=3, m=65536, p=4) off-thread. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
13	- **D-009 RBAC as data + partial-bound WrapSerializer masking:** code-defined `core_permissions` catalog, tenant-scoped `core_roles` + join tables; `require_permission(key)` dependency resolves effective permissions in one join query, TTL-cached 60 s keyed on (tenant, user, token_version); field masking via `Masked(tp, permission)` WrapSerializer reading a `current_permissions` ContextVar, masked fields excluded from Update schemas. Tenants can't invent keys no code checks. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
14	- **D-010 Split-phase audit capture in-transaction:** `before_flush` diffs updates/deletes from attribute history, `after_flush` captures inserts (generated PKs), `after_flush_postexec` writes one Core insert to append-only `core_audit_log` in the same transaction; per-dialect triggers (ATLAS_AUDIT_APPEND_ONLY) forbid update/delete; ORM bulk writes on audited models are hard errors. Audit is exactly as atomic as the change. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
15	- **D-011 In-process event bus, collect-then-dispatch in-transaction:** `publish()` buffers in session.info; `run_in_uow()` drains FIFO before commit, handlers share the session (cap 50, cycle error), any handler failure rolls back everything — goods issue without COGS can never commit. `events.py` becomes a sanctioned declarative cross-module import (STRUCTURE §5 amendment); swap path is an outbox bus behind the same Protocol. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
16	- **D-012 Document registry + flow links + gapless numbering (merged):** `core_documents` registry (nullable doc_no, partial unique index) with `DocumentMixin` NOT NULL document_id, `core_doc_links` edges traversed by one recursive CTE; numbers from `core_number_sequences` via atomic UPDATE...RETURNING, claimed only in the transaction that makes a document permanent (drafts numbered at posting) — so gaplessness falls out of ACID with no burned numbers. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
17	- **D-013 Idempotency by PK reservation + atomic route capture:** `core_idempotency_keys` PK(tenant, endpoint, key); guard inserts 'in_progress' in a separate committed transaction (concurrent duplicates collide), replays stored responses on completed+matching hash; the handler's `idem.capture(schema)` stages the completed UPDATE on the business session so replay record and document commit atomically — fail-closed if capture is forgotten. Required on every financial/stock-document endpoint. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
18	- **D-014 Keyset pagination + one error envelope + ATLAS_ token translation:** `{items, next_cursor, limit}` with base64url cursors fingerprinting sort+filters, expanded portable seek predicate, never OFFSET; all errors as `{error: {code, message, details, request_id}}` with dot-namespaced codes; a DBAPIError translator maps trigger tokens (ATLAS_PERIOD_CLOSED etc.) to envelope codes so DB backstops surface like service checks. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
19	- **D-015 Exact money via TypeDecorators (supersedes D-003's "plain Numeric"):** MoneyType/QuantityType (PG NUMERIC(18,6), SQLite INTEGER micro-units ×10^6) and RateType (20,10 / ×10^10); Decimal-only in Python, strings in JSON; quantize ROUND_HALF_UP to currency decimals at posting; single largest-remainder `allocate()` in new `core/money.py` (STRUCTURE §2 amendment); triggers do comparisons and SUMs only. Plain Numeric float-round-trips on SQLite and breaks exact trigger sums. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
20	- **D-016 Custom fields owned by core, not industry:** `core_custom_field_defs` registry + `validate_custom_fields()` + JSONB/JSON `custom_fields` column helper live in new `core/custom_fields.py` (STRUCTURE §2 amendment) — industry-module ownership would force upward imports from finance/inventory; templates and admin CRUD write defs through core services; flat scalar keys only, DECIMAL as strings, portable `.as_string()`-style JSON paths. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
21	- **D-017 Universal journal: one-side CHECK, two-flush posting, reversal-only:** `fin_journal_entries` (nullable entry_number claimed at posting) + `fin_journal_lines` with all CO dimensions, transaction+functional amount pairs, `ck_fin_journal_lines_one_side`; balance trigger on DRAFT→POSTED (ATLAS_UNBALANCED_ENTRY), immutability triggers (ATLAS_POSTED_IMMUTABLE) allowing only the reversal status mutation; posting mutates loaded lines then header across two flushes; residual functional cent absorbed largest-remainder (no rounding line). Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
22	- **D-018 Period close enforced by per-dialect triggers + service check:** `fin_fiscal_periods`; `trg_fin_entries_period_open` re-derives the period from posting_date on DRAFT→POSTED (plus an INSERT twin) and aborts ATLAS_PERIOD_CLOSED when no OPEN period covers the date — catching wrong-period-id service bugs; service raises 422 'finance.period_closed' first; close refuses while drafts exist in the period. Triggers are the only cross-table guard on both engines. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
23	- **D-019 FX: posting-time translation, realized at clearing, auto-reversing revaluation:** `fin_exchange_rates` (SPOT/CLOSING), `get_rate()` fails loud on missing rates; functional amounts frozen at posting (largest-remainder balancing); realized gain/loss posted inside the clearing entry via purpose-keyed `fin_posting_defaults`; `run_fx_revaluation` posts one FX_REVAL entry per (currency, account) and its next-period auto-reversal, validating up front that the next period is open. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
24	- **D-020 Inventory costing: moving average + FIFO, same-transaction COGS, no negative stock:** `inv_item_valuations` updated under `with_for_update` (SQLite no-ops it; single-writer lock suffices, pg-marked tests prove the PG path); FIFO via `inv_cost_layers` + `inv_layer_consumptions` with exact reversal replay; the event bus posts the COGS journal entry in the SAME transaction as the move — stock and GL can never diverge; negative stock forbidden by service + CHECKs. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.

Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
26	- **D-022 Single Alembic chain on both engines; migrations are the only schema source:** `create_all` banned even in tests (triggers live only in migrations); batch_alter_table everywhere + MetaData naming_convention; per-dialect trigger DDL side by side, re-executed after any batch-alter of a trigger-bearing table (SQLite copy-rebuild silently drops triggers); CI runs full suite on SQLite plus downgrade/upgrade and `-m pg` DB-guard subset on postgres:16. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.
27	- **D-023 Hand-written frontend types with a compile-time drift gate:** per-module `types.ts` mirrors Pydantic schemas (Decimal/date/UUID → string, enums → literal unions, Masked → `T | null`); committed `backend/openapi.json` (freshness pytest-asserted) feeds a gitignored openapi-typescript output checked by per-module `types.contract.ts` Equal-assertions in `npm run typecheck` — drift fails CI in both directions with zero runtime cost. Full spec: docs/architecture.md.

TEMPLATE`) so real commits — idempotency reservations, run_in_uow, numbering — work as in production and triggers exist; factories provision through real services; raw-SQL DB-guard tests pin the ATLAS_ tokens on both engines; tenancy suite auto-covers new mappers. 1	"""Async engine and session plumbing.
2	
3	Every engine the app touches (runtime, tests, migrations) is built via build_engine
4	or has enable_sqlite_foreign_keys attached, so the SQLite FK pragma backstop of
5	D-007 can never be silently absent.
6	"""
7	
8	from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
9	from typing import Any
10	
11	from sqlalchemy import Engine, event
12	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import (
13	    AsyncEngine,
14	    AsyncSession,
15	    async_sessionmaker,
16	    create_async_engine,
17	)
18	
19	from app.core.audit import install_audit_guards
20	from app.core.config import get_settings
21	from app.core.tenancy import install_tenancy_guards
22	
23	# Import side effect ON PURPOSE: every engine/session factory in app, tests and
24	# seed is built via this module, so importing it guarantees the D-007 + D-010 listeners
25	# exist before any session can be constructed. tenancy.py itself cannot self-install
26	# from models.py (import cycle), and main.py would leave direct-session users
27	# (tests, seed, alembic) unguarded.
28	#
29	# Order is load-bearing (D-010): tenancy first so its before_flush STAMPS tenant_id, then
30	# audit so its before_flush fires AFTER and reads a settled tenant_id. before_flush
31	# listeners fire in registration order, so this call order is the guarantee.
32	install_tenancy_guards()
33	install_audit_guards()
34	
35	
36	def _set_sqlite_fk_pragma(dbapi_connection: Any, connection_record: Any) -> None:
37	    cursor = dbapi_connection.cursor()
38	    cursor.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
39	    cursor.close()
40	
41	
42	def enable_sqlite_foreign_keys(engine: Engine) -> None:
43	    """SQLite enforces FK constraints only with this per-connection pragma (D-007)."""
44	    if engine.dialect.name == "sqlite":
45	        event.listen(engine, "connect", _set_sqlite_fk_pragma)
46	
47	
48	def build_engine(url: str, **kwargs: Any) -> AsyncEngine:
49	    """The single sanctioned way to create an engine; attaches the FK pragma listener."""
50	    engine = create_async_engine(url, **kwargs)
51	    enable_sqlite_foreign_keys(engine.sync_engine)
52	    return engine
53	
54	
55	def build_session_factory(engine: AsyncEngine) -> async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession]:
56	    return async_sessionmaker(engine, expire_on_commit=False)
57	
58	
59	engine = build_engine(get_settings().database_url)
60	session_factory = build_session_factory(engine)
61	
62	
63	async def get_session() -> AsyncIterator[AsyncSession]:
64	    """FastAPI dependency. Commits belong to the unit-of-work helper (later task);
65	    here: yield, roll back on exception, always close via the context manager."""
66	    async with session_factory() as session:
67	        try:
68	            yield session
69	        except Exception:
70	            await session.rollback()
71	            raise

1	"""D-007 tenancy enforcement: context, non-bypassable session filter, write stamping.
2	
3	Three of the four cooperating D-007 layers live here:
4	1. Context — the `current_tenant_id` ContextVar (set by core/deps.py after JWT
5	   validation from PLAN 3.3 on; by `tenant_context()` in tests and seed).
6	2. Read/write filtering — the `do_orm_execute` listener.
7	3. Write stamping — the `before_flush` listener.
8	The fourth layer (composite FKs + the SQLite FK pragma) lives in core/models.py
9	and core/db.py.
10	"""
11	
12	import uuid
13	from collections.abc import Iterator
14	from contextlib import contextmanager
15	from contextvars import ContextVar
16	from itertools import chain
17	
18	from sqlalchemy import event
19	from sqlalchemy.orm import ORMExecuteState, Session, with_loader_criteria
20	
21	from app.core.exceptions import TenancyError
22	from app.core.models import TenantMixin
23	
24	current_tenant_id: ContextVar[uuid.UUID | None] = ContextVar("current_tenant_id", default=None)
25	_system_context: ContextVar[bool] = ContextVar("system_context", default=False)
26	
27	
28	def get_current_tenant_id() -> uuid.UUID | None:
29	    """Active tenant id, fail-closed: raises unless a tenant context is set.
30	    Returns None only while system_context() is active."""
31	    tenant_id = current_tenant_id.get()
32	    if tenant_id is None and not _system_context.get():
33	        raise TenancyError("No tenant context is active")
34	    return tenant_id
35	
36	
37	@contextmanager
38	def tenant_context(tenant_id: uuid.UUID) -> Iterator[None]:
39	    """Run the block as one tenant (tests, seed transaction phase; request handling
40	    sets the ContextVar directly in core/deps.py with middleware reset, per D-007)."""
41	    token = current_tenant_id.set(tenant_id)
42	    try:
43	        yield
44	    finally:
45	        current_tenant_id.reset(token)
46	
47	
48	@contextmanager
49	def system_context() -> Iterator[None]:
50	    """Suspend tenant filtering and write stamping for the block.
51	
52	    Sanctioned in exactly four greppable app call sites (D-007):
53	    1. login user-lookup (core/auth, PLAN 3.3);
54	    2. tenant provisioning in modules/admin (PLAN 14.2);
55	    3. Alembic/seed provisioning phase (seed.py, PLAN 16);
56	    4. event-bus system-event replay (core/events, PLAN 3.6).
57	    Test fixtures may also use it (D-025 tenant_factory). Writers under system
58	    context must set tenant_id explicitly; the composite-FK backstop still applies.
59	    """
60	    token = _system_context.set(True)
61	    try:
62	        yield
63	    finally:
64	        _system_context.reset(token)
65	
66	
67	def _involves_tenant_scoped_entities(execute_state: ORMExecuteState) -> bool:
68	    # all_mappers inspects select() column descriptions / mapper entities AND the
69	    # bind mapper of ORM-enabled update()/delete() — the D-007 involvement rule.
70	    return any(issubclass(m.class_, TenantMixin) for m in execute_state.all_mappers)
71	
72	
73	def _filter_tenant_statements(execute_state: ORMExecuteState) -> None:
74	    """do_orm_execute listener: inject the tenant predicate into every ORM
75	    select/update/delete; fail-closed when tenant-scoped entities are touched
76	    without a tenant context."""
77	    if not execute_state.is_orm_statement:
78	        # Core statements bypass by design: sanctioned only inside core/ with
79	        # explicit tenant_id, bounded by the D-007 grep gate.
80	        return
81	    if execute_state.is_column_load or execute_state.is_relationship_load:
82	        # Refresh and lazy loads inherit the criteria propagated from their
83	        # originating statement; re-injecting here would break attribute refresh.
84	        return
85	    if not (execute_state.is_select or execute_state.is_update or execute_state.is_delete):
86	        return
87	    if _system_context.get():
88	        return
89	    tenant_id = current_tenant_id.get()
90	    if tenant_id is None:
91	        if _involves_tenant_scoped_entities(execute_state):
92	            raise TenancyError("Tenant-scoped statement executed without a tenant context")
93	        # Statements touching only non-tenant tables (Alembic bookkeeping, the
94	        # tenants root) legitimately run with no tenant context.
95	        return
96	    execute_state.statement = execute_state.statement.options(
97	        with_loader_criteria(
98	            TenantMixin,
99	            # The ContextVar is read above, in this per-execution listener — the
100	            # lambda-SQL system forbids invoking .get() inside the lambda itself.
101	            # track_closure_variables=False keeps the closure value out of the
102	            # statement cache key, so each execution binds the fresh tenant id
103	            # instead of baking in the first value seen (pinned by a test).
104	            lambda cls: cls.tenant_id == tenant_id,
105	            include_aliases=True,
106	            track_closure_variables=False,
107	        )
108	    )
109	
110	
111	def _stamp_tenant_on_flush(session: Session, flush_context: object, instances: object) -> None:
112	    """before_flush listener: stamp tenant_id on new tenant-scoped instances and
113	    reject any new/dirty instance whose tenant_id differs from the context."""
114	    if _system_context.get():
115	        # Provisioning/seed/system writes set tenant_id explicitly; the composite
116	        # FK backstop still rejects ids that do not exist in adm_tenants.
117	        return
118	    active = current_tenant_id.get()
119	    for obj in chain(session.new, session.dirty):
120	        if not isinstance(obj, TenantMixin):
121	            continue
122	        if active is None:
123	            raise TenancyError("Tenant-scoped instance flushed without a tenant context")
124	        if obj.tenant_id is None:
125	            obj.tenant_id = active
126	        elif obj.tenant_id != active:
127	            raise TenancyError(
128	                "Instance tenant_id differs from the active tenant context",
129	                code="tenancy.tenant_mismatch",
130	            )
131	
132	
133	def install_tenancy_guards() -> None:
134	    """Attach both listeners to the sync Session class — AsyncSession proxies it,
135	    so every execute call and relationship load is covered. Idempotent so repeated
136	    calls cannot double-register. Invoked at import time of app.core.db: every
137	    engine/session factory in app, tests and seed is built from that module, so no
138	    session can exist unguarded (models.py cannot host the call — this module
139	    imports TenantMixin from it, which would be an import cycle)."""
140	    if not event.contains(Session, "do_orm_execute", _filter_tenant_statements):
141	        event.listen(Session, "do_orm_execute", _filter_tenant_statements)
142	    if not event.contains(Session, "before_flush", _stamp_tenant_on_flush):
143	        event.listen(Session, "before_flush", _stamp_tenant_on_flush)
144

1	"""FastAPI dependencies (D-008 get_current_user, D-007 production ContextVar setter).
2	
3	This is the ONE place that sets `current_tenant_id` for the request lifecycle from a
4	validated access token; the pure-ASGI middleware in app.main resets it in a finally
5	block so request A's tenant never leaks to request B on the same worker.
6	"""
7	
8	import uuid
9	from dataclasses import dataclass
10	from typing import Annotated
11	
12	from fastapi import Depends
13	from fastapi.security import HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, HTTPBearer
14	from sqlalchemy import select
15	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
16	
17	from app.core.audit import actor_user_id_ctx
18	from app.core.auth import decode_token
19	from app.core.config import get_settings
20	from app.core.db import get_session
21	from app.core.exceptions import AuthError
22	from app.core.models import User
23	from app.core.rbac import current_permissions, resolve_permissions
24	from app.core.tenancy import current_tenant_id
25	
26	# get_session / get_settings are re-exported so routers depend on a single core.deps
27	# surface rather than reaching into core.db / core.config directly.
28	__all__ = [
29	    "CurrentUser",
30	    "CurrentUserDep",
31	    "SessionDep",
32	    "get_current_user",
33	    "get_session",
34	    "get_settings",
35	]
36	
37	# auto_error=False: a missing/blank header must surface as the D-014 auth envelope
38	# (AuthError -> 401), not Starlette's bare 403 HTTPException.
39	_bearer_scheme = HTTPBearer(auto_error=False)
40	
41	# Annotated dependency aliases: the modern FastAPI idiom that keeps Depends() out of
42	# parameter defaults (ruff B008) and lets routers share one typed handle.
43	SessionDep = Annotated[AsyncSession, Depends(get_session)]
44	_CredentialsDep = Annotated[HTTPAuthorizationCredentials | None, Depends(_bearer_scheme)]
45	
46	
47	@dataclass(frozen=True)
48	class CurrentUser:
49	    """Resolved request principal (D-008/D-009). `permissions` is the effective key set
50	    resolved by RBAC (one join query, cached 60s)."""
51	
52	    user_id: uuid.UUID
53	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID
54	    permissions: frozenset[str]
55	    token_version: int
56	
57	
58	async def get_current_user(
59	    credentials: _CredentialsDep,
60	    session: SessionDep,
61	) -> CurrentUser:
62	    if credentials is None:
63	        raise AuthError(message="Missing bearer token", code="auth.invalid_token")
64	
65	    claims = decode_token(credentials.credentials, expected_typ="access")
66	    try:
67	        user_id = uuid.UUID(claims["sub"])
68	        tenant_id = uuid.UUID(claims["tenant_id"])
69	        claim_version = int(claims["ver"])
70	    except (KeyError, ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
71	        raise AuthError(message="Invalid token", code="auth.invalid_token") from exc
72	
73	    # Set the tenancy ContextVar FROM the validated token (D-007 production setter):
74	    # the user lookup below then runs under the token's tenant, so a tampered
75	    # tenant_id can only ever resolve a user that actually belongs to that tenant —
76	    # cross-tenant access is impossible. The middleware resets this in a finally block.
77	    current_tenant_id.set(tenant_id)
78	
79	    user = (
80	        await session.execute(select(User).where(User.id == user_id))
81	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
82	    if user is None or not user.is_active:
83	        raise AuthError(message="Invalid token", code="auth.invalid_token")
84	    if user.token_version != claim_version:
85	        # Stale token after a "revoke everything" bump (D-008).
86	        raise AuthError(message="Invalid token", code="auth.invalid_token")
87	
88	    # RBAC resolution (D-009): one join query, memoized 60s on
89	    # (tenant_id, user_id, token_version). Runs under the tenant context set above, so
90	    # the user_roles/role_permissions rows are already tenant-filtered.
91	    permissions = await resolve_permissions(
92	        session, user.id, user.tenant_id, user.token_version
93	    )
94	    # Serialization-time masking (D-009) reads this ContextVar; the middleware resets it
95	    # in a finally block alongside current_tenant_id so it never leaks across requests.
96	    current_permissions.set(permissions)
97	    # D-010 audit context: now that the principal is known, stamp the actor onto every
98	    # audit row this request writes. The middleware seeded it None (system) and resets it.
99	    actor_user_id_ctx.set(user.id)
100	
101	    return CurrentUser(
102	        user_id=user.id,
103	        tenant_id=user.tenant_id,
104	        permissions=permissions,
105	        token_version=user.token_version,
106	    )
107	
108	
109	CurrentUserDep = Annotated[CurrentUser, Depends(get_current_user)]

1	"""AtlasError hierarchy rendered as the D-014 error envelope by handlers in app.main.
2	
3	This file also owns the D-014 DB-guard translation: trigger-raised `ATLAS_*` tokens are
4	mapped to envelope codes here so the DB backstops surface through the SAME envelope as
5	service-level checks. Kept in this file (not a new core/db_errors.py) because the map is a
6	small dict and STRUCTURE §8.1 prefers extending an existing home; promote to its own file
7	only if the table grows past a screenful.
8	"""
9	
10	from typing import Any
11	
12	from sqlalchemy.exc import DBAPIError
13	
14	
15	class AtlasError(Exception):
16	    """Base for every error the API surfaces deliberately. Codes are machine-readable
17	    and dot-namespaced (generic: common.*; domain rules: e.g. finance.period_closed)."""
18	
19	    def __init__(
20	        self,
21	        code: str,
22	        message: str,
23	        status_code: int = 400,
24	        details: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
25	    ) -> None:
26	        super().__init__(message)
27	        self.code = code
28	        self.message = message
29	        self.status_code = status_code
30	        self.details = details
31	
32	
33	class NotFoundError(AtlasError):
34	    def __init__(
35	        self,
36	        message: str = "Resource not found",
37	        code: str = "common.not_found",
38	        details: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
39	    ) -> None:
40	        super().__init__(code=code, message=message, status_code=404, details=details)
41	
42	
43	class ValidationFailedError(AtlasError):
44	    def __init__(
45	        self,
46	        message: str = "Validation failed",
47	        code: str = "common.validation_error",
48	        details: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
49	    ) -> None:
50	        super().__init__(code=code, message=message, status_code=422, details=details)
51	
52	
53	class ConflictError(AtlasError):
54	    def __init__(
55	        self,
56	        message: str = "Conflict with existing state",
57	        code: str = "common.conflict",
58	        details: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
59	    ) -> None:
60	        super().__init__(code=code, message=message, status_code=409, details=details)
61	
62	
63	class AuthError(AtlasError):
64	    def __init__(
65	        self,
66	        message: str = "Invalid credentials",
67	        code: str = "auth.invalid_credentials",
68	        details: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
69	    ) -> None:
70	        super().__init__(code=code, message=message, status_code=401, details=details)
71	
72	
73	class PermissionDeniedError(AtlasError):
74	    def __init__(
75	        self,
76	        message: str = "Permission denied",
77	        code: str = "common.permission_denied",
78	        details: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
79	    ) -> None:
80	        super().__init__(code=code, message=message, status_code=403, details=details)
81	
82	
83	class TenancyError(AtlasError):
84	    def __init__(
85	        self,
86	        message: str = "Tenant context missing or mismatched",
87	        code: str = "tenancy.context_missing",
88	        details: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
89	    ) -> None:
90	        super().__init__(code=code, message=message, status_code=403, details=details)
91	
92	
93	# --- D-014 DB-guard translation (trigger token -> envelope) --------------------
94	#
95	# Table-driven so future backstops (ATLAS_PERIOD_CLOSED, ATLAS_POSTED_IMMUTABLE,
96	# ATLAS_UNBALANCED_ENTRY) plug in by adding one row. SQLite RAISE(ABORT) surfaces as
97	# IntegrityError and asyncpg plpgsql RAISE surfaces differently, but both are subclasses
98	# of DBAPIError and both carry the token in str(exc) — so substring matching on the base
99	# class covers both engines (D-022 pins it on each).
100	#
101	# DEVIATION from D-014's literal table: D-014 maps ATLAS_AUDIT_APPEND_ONLY ->
102	# internal_error 500; PLAN 3.5 binds it to 409 / "audit.append_only" (an append-only
103	# write is a client-visible conflict, not an opaque server fault), so this map follows
104	# the task. Finance tokens below are pre-registered for PLAN 4 and keep D-014's codes.
105	DB_GUARD_TOKEN_MAP: dict[str, tuple[int, str]] = {
106	    "ATLAS_AUDIT_APPEND_ONLY": (409, "audit.append_only"),
107	    "ATLAS_PERIOD_CLOSED": (422, "finance.period_closed"),
108	    "ATLAS_POSTED_IMMUTABLE": (422, "finance.entry_immutable"),
109	    "ATLAS_UNBALANCED_ENTRY": (422, "finance.journal_unbalanced"),
110	}
111	
112	
113	def translate_db_guard_error(exc: DBAPIError) -> AtlasError | None:
114	    """Map a trigger-raised ATLAS_* token in a DBAPIError to an AtlasError, or None if the
115	    error carries no known token (then it is a genuine integrity/operational failure and
116	    the catch-all 500 handler owns it). Matching is on the full message text because the
117	    token is embedded in the raised exception string on both engines."""
118	    message = str(exc.orig) if exc.orig is not None else str(exc)
119	    for token, (status_code, code) in DB_GUARD_TOKEN_MAP.items():
120	        if token in message:
121	            return AtlasError(code=code, message=token, status_code=status_code)
122	    return None

1	"""D-011 domain-event bus: collect-then-dispatch, in the SAME transaction.
2	
3	Three pieces, exactly as D-011 prescribes:
4	
5	* ``DomainEvent`` — a frozen Pydantic v2 base. Each subclass declares a ClassVar
6	  ``key`` (module-prefixed past-tense string, e.g. ``'sales.order.shipped'``) and
7	  carries ``tenant_id`` + ``occurred_at`` plus its own payload fields. Events are
8	  PLAIN DATA — no behaviour — so a publishing module's ``events.py`` is a sanctioned
9	  cross-module import (STRUCTURE §5 amendment, D-011): a subscriber in another module's
10	  ``handlers.py`` imports the typed event class without importing any logic.
11	
12	* The subscription registry — ``subscribe(key, handler)`` and the ``@on(EventClass)``
13	  decorator a module's ``handlers.py`` calls at import time; ``clear_subscriptions()``
14	  / ``subscriptions_snapshot()`` / ``restore_subscriptions()`` give the tests a clean
15	  registry per case so module-registered handlers in later phases never leak.
16	
17	* ``InProcessEventBus`` behind the ``EventBus`` Protocol, plus the single shared
18	  unit-of-work drain point ``run_in_uow``:
19	  - ``publish(session, event)`` appends to a FIFO buffer in ``session.info`` — NO
20	    immediate dispatch, so handlers observe the publisher's settled aggregate state.
21	  - ``run_in_uow(session, work)`` runs the business ``work``, then drains the buffer
22	    breadth-first (FIFO), invoking each handler with the SAME session so its writes
23	    land in the SAME transaction, THEN commits. A handler may publish further events;
24	    those are drained too, up to ``MAX_DISPATCHES_PER_UOW`` total, then ``EventCycleError``.
25	    ANY exception — business work or any handler — rolls the whole transaction back and
26	    re-raises: deliberately NO per-handler isolation (if the COGS posting fails, the
27	    goods issue must not commit). This is the load-bearing all-or-nothing invariant.
28	
29	**Handler order** is deterministic: per event key, handlers fire in registration order
30	(module import order in main.py's app factory); events fire in publish (FIFO) order.
31	
32	**Tenant context** (D-007): handlers run UNDER the trigger's already-active tenant
33	context, so their tenant-scoped reads/writes are filtered and stamped like any other
34	write. A handler doing system-level work wraps it in ``system_context()`` itself (the
35	D-007 site-4 "bus system-event replay" seam) — the bus does not change context for it.
36	
37	**Audit** (D-010): handler writes share the session, so the before_flush/after_flush
38	audit listeners capture and tenant-stamp them automatically — no extra wiring (proven
39	by tests/core/test_events.py).
40	
41	**Swap path:** the in-transaction semantics ARE the contract, expressed by the
42	``EventBus`` Protocol. A future ``TransactionalOutboxBus`` implements the same Protocol,
43	writing ``core_event_outbox`` rows in the same transaction for an external relay, with
44	zero business-logic changes. The outbox TABLE is introduced THEN (a later PLAN task),
45	not now — v1 ships only the in-process bus.
46	"""
47	
48	import uuid
49	from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
50	from datetime import UTC, datetime
51	from typing import ClassVar, Protocol, runtime_checkable
52	
53	from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field
54	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
55	
56	from app.core.exceptions import AtlasError
57	
58	# Hard ceiling on handler dispatches per unit of work (D-011): handlers may publish
59	# further events, drained in the same uow, but a cycle (A -> B -> A) or a runaway fan-out
60	# would otherwise hold the transaction open forever. At the cap we raise rather than spin.
61	MAX_DISPATCHES_PER_UOW = 50
62	
63	# FIFO buffer of not-yet-dispatched events, keyed in session.info so it is per-session
64	# (per-transaction) and never shared across requests.
65	_BUFFER_KEY = "pending_events"
66	
67	
68	class EventCycleError(AtlasError):
69	    """A unit of work dispatched more than MAX_DISPATCHES_PER_UOW events — almost always
70	    a handler-publish cycle. Surfaced as a 500 (a server-side wiring fault, not client
71	    input) and, like every handler failure, rolls the whole transaction back (D-011)."""
72	
73	    def __init__(self, dispatched: int) -> None:
74	        super().__init__(
75	            code="events.cycle_detected",
76	            message=(
77	                f"Event dispatch exceeded the per-transaction cap of "
78	                f"{MAX_DISPATCHES_PER_UOW} (dispatched {dispatched}); likely a handler "
79	                "publish cycle."
80	            ),
81	            status_code=500,
82	        )
83	
84	
85	class DomainEvent(BaseModel):
86	    """Base for every domain event (D-011). Frozen + plain data, no behaviour.
87	
88	    Subclasses declare their string key and payload:
89	
90	        class SalesOrderShipped(DomainEvent):
91	            key: ClassVar[str] = "sales.order.shipped"
92	            order_id: uuid.UUID
93	
94	    ``key`` is a ClassVar (one value per event TYPE, not a per-instance field) so it is
95	    not part of the payload schema; ``tenant_id`` + ``occurred_at`` are carried on every
96	    event. ``frozen=True`` makes instances immutable — an event is a fact that happened.
97	    """
98	
99	    model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)
100	
101	    # Declared on the base as a sentinel; every concrete subclass overrides it. Kept as a
102	    # ClassVar so Pydantic does not treat it as a payload field.
103	    key: ClassVar[str] = ""
104	
105	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID
106	    occurred_at: datetime = Field(default_factory=lambda: datetime.now(UTC))
107	
108	
109	# A handler is an async callable taking the shared session and the event, returning None.
110	# It runs before commit, inside the trigger's transaction and tenant context (D-011/D-007).
111	Handler = Callable[[AsyncSession, DomainEvent], Awaitable[None]]
112	
113	# Registry: event key -> handlers in registration order. Module import order (main.py's
114	# app factory) therefore fixes handler order deterministically (D-011).
115	_subscriptions: dict[str, list[Handler]] = {}
116	
117	
118	def subscribe(event_key: str, handler: Handler) -> None:
119	    """Register ``handler`` for ``event_key``. Called by a module's handlers.py at import,
120	    directly or via the ``@on`` decorator. Order of registration = dispatch order."""
121	    _subscriptions.setdefault(event_key, []).append(handler)
122	
123	
124	def on(event_type: type[DomainEvent]) -> Callable[[Handler], Handler]:
125	    """Decorator form of subscribe, keyed off the event CLASS so handlers.py stays typed:
126	
127	        @on(SalesOrderShipped)
128	        async def post_cogs(session: AsyncSession, event: SalesOrderShipped) -> None: ...
129	
130	    Returns the handler unchanged so it can still be called/tested directly."""
131	
132	    def decorator(handler: Handler) -> Handler:
133	        subscribe(event_type.key, handler)
134	        return handler
135	
136	    return decorator
137	
138	
139	def handlers_for(event_key: str) -> tuple[Handler, ...]:
140	    """Registered handlers for a key, in registration order (empty tuple if none)."""
141	    return tuple(_subscriptions.get(event_key, ()))
142	
143	
144	def clear_subscriptions() -> None:
145	    """Drop every registration. The autouse test fixture calls this so handlers a module
146	    registers at import in later phases cannot leak between tests (D-025 isolation)."""
147	    _subscriptions.clear()
148	
149	
150	def subscriptions_snapshot() -> dict[str, list[Handler]]:
151	    """Deep-ish copy of the registry for save/restore around a test that mutates it."""
152	    return {key: list(value) for key, value in _subscriptions.items()}
153	
154	
155	def restore_subscriptions(snapshot: dict[str, list[Handler]]) -> None:
156	    """Replace the registry with a previously taken snapshot."""
157	    _subscriptions.clear()
158	    _subscriptions.update({key: list(value) for key, value in snapshot.items()})
159	
160	
161	def _buffer(session: AsyncSession) -> list[DomainEvent]:
162	    return session.info.setdefault(_BUFFER_KEY, [])
163	
164	
165	@runtime_checkable
166	class EventBus(Protocol):
167	    """The swappable contract (D-011). The in-transaction semantics live in ``run_in_uow``,
168	    not here, so any implementation (in-process now, a transactional-outbox bus later)
169	    publishes the same way and business logic never changes. ``publish`` buffers; it does
170	    NOT dispatch — dispatch is owned by the single ``run_in_uow`` drain point."""
171	
172	    def publish(self, session: AsyncSession, event: DomainEvent) -> None: ...
173	
174	
175	class InProcessEventBus:
176	    """The only EventBus implementation in v1 (D-011). ``publish`` appends to the per-session
177	    FIFO buffer; the buffer is drained by ``run_in_uow`` after the business work and before
178	    commit, so handlers run synchronously in the trigger's transaction."""
179	
180	    def publish(self, session: AsyncSession, event: DomainEvent) -> None:
181	        _buffer(session).append(event)
182	
183	
184	# Module-level singleton: services import this and call ``bus.publish(session, event)``.
185	# A later outbox bus replaces THIS binding (same Protocol) and nothing else moves.
186	bus: EventBus = InProcessEventBus()
187	
188	
189	def publish(session: AsyncSession, event: DomainEvent) -> None:
190	    """Convenience free function delegating to the active bus, so callers can
191	    ``from app.core.events import publish`` without reaching for the singleton."""
192	    bus.publish(session, event)
193	
194	
195	async def _drain_and_dispatch(session: AsyncSession) -> None:
196	    """Pop buffered events FIFO and run their handlers, sharing ``session``. Handlers may
197	    publish more events (appended to the same buffer); we keep draining breadth-first up to
198	    MAX_DISPATCHES_PER_UOW total dispatches, then raise EventCycleError. A handler raising
199	    propagates — run_in_uow's caller rolls the whole transaction back (D-011: no isolation).
200	    """
201	    buffer = _buffer(session)
202	    dispatched = 0
203	    while buffer:
204	        event = buffer.pop(0)  # FIFO: oldest first
205	        for handler in handlers_for(event.key):
206	            if dispatched >= MAX_DISPATCHES_PER_UOW:
207	                raise EventCycleError(dispatched)
208	            await handler(session, event)
209	            dispatched += 1
210	    # Defensive: an event with no handler still counts toward nothing; a cap breach can
211	    # only happen above. Clearing the (now empty) key keeps session.info tidy.
212	    session.info.pop(_BUFFER_KEY, None)
213	
214	
215	async def run_in_uow(
216	    session: AsyncSession,
217	    work: Callable[[], Awaitable[None]] | Awaitable[None],
218	) -> None:
219	    """The single sanctioned unit-of-work helper (D-011). Used by the request session
220	    dependency (core/deps), by seed.py and by CLI flows, so HTTP, seed and tests get
221	    IDENTICAL event semantics.
222	
223	    Sequence: run ``work`` (the business mutation that publishes events) -> drain the
224	    buffered events FIFO and run their handlers on the SAME session (so handler effects,
225	    e.g. a COGS journal, are in the same transaction as the trigger, e.g. the stock
226	    issue) -> commit. If the business work OR any handler raises (or the cascade cap is
227	    hit), roll the WHOLE transaction back and re-raise — the trigger's own writes do not
228	    persist. Handlers run under the trigger's active tenant context (D-007); nothing here
229	    changes it.
230	
231	    ``work`` may be a coroutine object or a zero-arg callable returning an awaitable, so
232	    both ``run_in_uow(session, service_coro)`` and ``run_in_uow(session, lambda: ...)``
233	    read naturally at call sites.
234	    """
235	    try:
236	        awaitable = work() if callable(work) else work
237	        await awaitable
238	        await _drain_and_dispatch(session)
239	        await session.commit()
240	    except Exception:
241	        await session.rollback()
242	        # Drop any partially drained / leftover buffer so the next uow on this session
243	        # (tests reuse one session) starts clean.
244	        session.info.pop(_BUFFER_KEY, None)
245	        raise

1	"""App factory and app-level plumbing: request id, CORS, error envelope, health."""
2	
3	import logging
4	import uuid
5	from typing import Any
6	
7	from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
8	from fastapi.exceptions import RequestValidationError
9	from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
10	from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
11	from sqlalchemy.exc import DBAPIError
12	from starlette.datastructures import MutableHeaders
13	from starlette.exceptions import HTTPException as StarletteHTTPException
14	from starlette.types import ASGIApp, Message, Receive, Scope, Send
15	
16	from app.core.audit import actor_user_id_ctx, request_id_ctx, request_ip_ctx
17	from app.core.config import Settings, get_settings
18	from app.core.exceptions import AtlasError, translate_db_guard_error
19	from app.core.rbac import current_permissions
20	from app.core.schemas import ErrorBody, ErrorEnvelope
21	from app.core.security_router import router as security_router
22	from app.core.tenancy import current_tenant_id
23	
24	logger = logging.getLogger("atlas")
25	
26	API_PREFIX = "/api/v1"
27	
28	# request_id lives in the audit module (core/audit.py owns the request-context ContextVars);
29	# re-exported under the historical name so existing callers/tests keep one import.
30	request_id_var = request_id_ctx
31	
32	
33	def _client_ip(scope: Scope, trust_proxy: bool) -> str | None:
34	    """Audited client IP (D-010). Default: the raw transport peer (scope['client']). Only
35	    when ATLAS_TRUST_PROXY is on do we honor the LEFT-MOST X-Forwarded-For hop — otherwise a
36	    client could spoof its own audited IP just by sending the header."""
37	    if trust_proxy:
38	        for raw_name, raw_value in scope.get("headers", ()):
39	            if raw_name == b"x-forwarded-for":
40	                first_hop = raw_value.decode("latin-1").split(",")[0].strip()
41	                if first_hop:
42	                    return first_hop
43	    client = scope.get("client")
44	    return client[0] if client else None
45	
46	
47	class RequestIdMiddleware:
48	    """Pure-ASGI: one uuid4-hex request id per request, exposed via ContextVar,
49	    request.state and the X-Request-ID response header.
50	
51	    It ALSO owns the D-007 tenancy-ContextVar reset, the D-009 current_permissions reset,
52	    and the D-010 audit-context (request_id, request_ip, actor_user_id) lifecycle:
53	    get_current_user sets the tenant/permissions/actor vars directly (no context manager),
54	    so this middleware captures reset tokens in a finally block — otherwise request A's
55	    context would leak into request B reusing the same worker/task. request_id and
56	    request_ip are seeded here at the edge; actor_user_id starts None (system/unauth) and is
57	    filled by get_current_user once the principal is known. All are reset on the way out, so
58	    the worker always restarts at the defaults."""
59	
60	    def __init__(self, app: ASGIApp, trust_proxy: bool) -> None:
61	        self.app = app
62	        self.trust_proxy = trust_proxy
63	
64	    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
65	        if scope["type"] != "http":
66	            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
67	            return
68	        request_id = uuid.uuid4().hex
69	        scope.setdefault("state", {})["request_id"] = request_id
70	        token = request_id_var.set(request_id)
71	        ip_token = request_ip_ctx.set(_client_ip(scope, self.trust_proxy))
72	        actor_token = actor_user_id_ctx.set(None)
73	        tenant_token = current_tenant_id.set(None)
74	        permissions_token = current_permissions.set(frozenset())
75	
76	        async def send_with_request_id(message: Message) -> None:
77	            if message["type"] == "http.response.start":
78	                MutableHeaders(scope=message)["X-Request-ID"] = request_id
79	            await send(message)
80	
81	        try:
82	            await self.app(scope, receive, send_with_request_id)
83	        finally:
84	            current_permissions.reset(permissions_token)
85	            current_tenant_id.reset(tenant_token)
86	            actor_user_id_ctx.reset(actor_token)
87	            request_ip_ctx.reset(ip_token)
88	            request_id_var.reset(token)
89	
90	
91	def _request_id(request: Request) -> str | None:
92	    # The ContextVar is already reset when the catch-all handler runs (Starlette's
93	    # ServerErrorMiddleware sits outside RequestIdMiddleware), hence the state fallback.
94	    return request_id_var.get() or getattr(request.state, "request_id", None)
95	
96	
97	def _error_response(
98	    request: Request,
99	    status_code: int,
100	    code: str,
101	    message: str,
102	    details: list[Any] | dict[str, Any] | None = None,
103	) -> JSONResponse:
104	    request_id = _request_id(request)
105	    envelope = ErrorEnvelope(
106	        error=ErrorBody(code=code, message=message, details=details, request_id=request_id)
107	    )
108	    # Set the header here too: 500 responses bypass RequestIdMiddleware's send wrapper.
109	    headers = {"X-Request-ID": request_id} if request_id else None
110	    return JSONResponse(status_code=status_code, content=envelope.model_dump(), headers=headers)
111	
112	
113	async def _handle_atlas_error(request: Request, exc: AtlasError) -> JSONResponse:
114	    return _error_response(request, exc.status_code, exc.code, exc.message, exc.details)
115	
116	
117	async def _handle_http_exception(request: Request, exc: StarletteHTTPException) -> JSONResponse:
118	    code = "common.not_found" if exc.status_code == 404 else "common.http_error"
119	    return _error_response(request, exc.status_code, code, str(exc.detail))
120	
121	
122	async def _handle_validation_error(
123	    request: Request, exc: RequestValidationError
124	) -> JSONResponse:
125	    details = [
126	        {
127	            "field": ".".join(str(part) for part in err.get("loc", ())),
128	            "message": err.get("msg", ""),
129	            "type": err.get("type", ""),
130	        }
131	        for err in exc.errors()
132	    ]
133	    return _error_response(
134	        request, 422, "common.validation_error", "Request validation failed", details
135	    )
136	
137	
138	async def _handle_db_guard_error(request: Request, exc: DBAPIError) -> JSONResponse:
139	    # D-014: a DB trigger that raised an ATLAS_* token surfaces through the same envelope
140	    # as service-level checks (e.g. ATLAS_AUDIT_APPEND_ONLY -> 409 audit.append_only). A
141	    # DBAPIError WITHOUT a known token is a genuine integrity/operational fault — log it and
142	    # return the opaque 500 like any unexpected error, never leaking raw DB text.
143	    translated = translate_db_guard_error(exc)
144	    if translated is not None:
145	        return _error_response(
146	            request, translated.status_code, translated.code, translated.message
147	        )
148	    logger.exception("Database error (request_id=%s)", _request_id(request), exc_info=exc)
149	    return _error_response(request, 500, "common.internal_error", "Internal server error")
150	
151	
152	async def _handle_unexpected_error(request: Request, exc: Exception) -> JSONResponse:
153	    # Log with request id; never leak the traceback into the response body.
154	    logger.exception("Unhandled error (request_id=%s)", _request_id(request), exc_info=exc)
155	    return _error_response(request, 500, "common.internal_error", "Internal server error")
156	
157	
158	def create_app(settings: Settings | None = None) -> FastAPI:
159	    settings = settings or get_settings()
160	    logging.basicConfig(level=settings.log_level.upper())
161	
162	    app = FastAPI(
163	        title="Atlas ERP",
164	        version="0.1.0",
165	        openapi_url=f"{API_PREFIX}/openapi.json",
166	        docs_url=f"{API_PREFIX}/docs",
167	        redoc_url=None,
168	    )
169	
170	    app.add_middleware(
171	        CORSMiddleware,
172	        allow_origins=settings.cors_origins,
173	        allow_credentials=True,
174	        allow_methods=["*"],
175	        allow_headers=["*"],
176	    )
177	    # Added last == outermost user middleware: the request id exists for everything
178	    # below it, including CORS rejections.
179	    app.add_middleware(RequestIdMiddleware, trust_proxy=settings.trust_proxy)
180	
181	    app.add_exception_handler(AtlasError, _handle_atlas_error)
182	    app.add_exception_handler(StarletteHTTPException, _handle_http_exception)
183	    app.add_exception_handler(RequestValidationError, _handle_validation_error)
184	    # DBAPIError is more specific than Exception, so Starlette dispatches DB-guard tokens
185	    # (D-014) here before falling through to the catch-all 500 below.
186	    app.add_exception_handler(DBAPIError, _handle_db_guard_error)
187	    app.add_exception_handler(Exception, _handle_unexpected_error)
188	
189	    @app.get(f"{API_PREFIX}/health")
190	    async def health() -> dict[str, str]:
191	        return {"status": "ok", "env": settings.env}
192	
193	    # Core platform auth endpoints (D-008): login/refresh/logout/me at /api/v1/auth.
194	    app.include_router(security_router)
195	
196	    return app
197	
198	
199	app = create_app()

3	JUSTIFIED ADDITION to core: auth endpoints are cross-cutting platform, not a business
4	module — STRUCTURE's module list has no `auth`, and they don't belong to any single
5	module. Routers normally live in modules/, so this is a deliberate, recorded exception
6	(prefix /api/v1/auth). Logic stays thin: it composes core/auth primitives, the
7	admin provisioning service, and the RefreshSession model.
8	"""

10	import uuid
11	from datetime import datetime, timedelta
12	
13	from fastapi import APIRouter, Request, Response
14	from sqlalchemy import select, update
15	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
16	
17	from app.core import auth
18	from app.core.config import get_settings
19	from app.core.deps import CurrentUserDep, SessionDep
20	from app.core.exceptions import AuthError
21	from app.core.models import RefreshSession, User
22	from app.core.schemas import LoginRequest, MeResponse, TokenResponse
23	from app.core.tenancy import current_tenant_id, system_context
24	from app.modules.admin.service import find_tenant_by_slug, find_user_by_email
25	
26	router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/v1/auth", tags=["auth"])
27	
28	# Cookie scoped to the refresh endpoints only (D-008): the access token is never a
29	# cookie, so the SPA holds it in memory; the refresh cookie is invisible to JS.
30	_COOKIE_NAME = "atlas_refresh"
31	_COOKIE_PATH = "/api/v1/auth"
32	# Grace window for benign multi-tab refresh races (D-008): a refresh presenting the
33	# immediately-previous jti within this window rotates instead of revoking the family.
34	_GRACE_SECONDS = 10
35	
36	
37	def _set_refresh_cookie(response: Response, refresh_token: str, max_age: int) -> None:
38	    response.set_cookie(
39	        key=_COOKIE_NAME,
40	        value=refresh_token,
41	        max_age=max_age,
42	        path=_COOKIE_PATH,
43	        httponly=True,
44	        secure=True,
45	        samesite="strict",
46	    )
47	
48	
49	def _clear_refresh_cookie(response: Response) -> None:
50	    response.delete_cookie(key=_COOKIE_NAME, path=_COOKIE_PATH, httponly=True, secure=True)
51	
52	
53	def _refresh_ttl_seconds() -> int:
54	    return get_settings().jwt_refresh_ttl_seconds
55	
56	
57	def _issue_tokens(
58	    response: Response,
59	    user_id: uuid.UUID,
60	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
61	    sid: uuid.UUID,
62	    token_version: int,
63	    now: datetime,
64	) -> tuple[TokenResponse, str]:
65	    """Mint a fresh access+refresh pair and set the refresh cookie. Returns the body
66	    and the new refresh jti (caller stores its hash as the session's current jti)."""
67	    access_token = auth.encode_access(user_id, tenant_id, sid, token_version, now=now)
68	    refresh_token = auth.encode_refresh(user_id, tenant_id, sid, now=now)
69	    _set_refresh_cookie(response, refresh_token, _refresh_ttl_seconds())
70	    new_jti = auth.decode_token(refresh_token, expected_typ="refresh")["jti"]
71	    return TokenResponse(access_token=access_token), new_jti

73	
74	@router.post("/login", response_model=TokenResponse)
75	async def login(
76	    payload: LoginRequest,
77	    request: Request,
78	    response: Response,
79	    session: SessionDep,
80	) -> TokenResponse:
81	    # Tenant + user resolution runs under system_context (D-007 site 1) — no trusted
82	    # tenant context exists yet. Generic 401 for every failure so we never reveal
83	    # whether the tenant, the email, or the password was wrong.
84	    tenant = await find_tenant_by_slug(session, payload.tenant_slug)
85	    if tenant is None or not tenant.is_active:
86	        raise AuthError()
87	    user = await find_user_by_email(session, tenant.id, payload.email)
88	    if user is None or not user.is_active:
89	        raise AuthError()
90	    if not await auth.verify_password_async(user.password_hash, payload.password):
91	        raise AuthError()
92	
93	    # Upgrade the stored hash if the argon2 parameters strengthened since it was made.
94	    # Mutate the LOADED object, not an ORM bulk update(): the D-010 audit bulk-write guard
95	    # forbids ORM update()/delete() on AuditMixin models (User is audited). password_hash is
96	    # in User.__audit_exclude__, so this flush writes no audit row — credentials never leak
97	    # into the trail (D-010 v1 policy: mutate auditable entities via loaded objects).
98	    if auth.needs_rehash(user.password_hash):
99	        user.password_hash = await auth.hash_password_async(payload.password)
100	
101	    now = auth.now_utc()
102	    sid = uuid.uuid4()
103	    body, new_jti = _issue_tokens(response, user.id, tenant.id, sid, user.token_version, now)
104	
105	    with system_context():
106	        session.add(
107	            RefreshSession(
108	                id=sid,
109	                tenant_id=tenant.id,
110	                user_id=user.id,
111	                current_jti_hash=auth.sha256_hex(new_jti),
112	                issued_at=now,
113	                last_used_at=now,
114	                expires_at=now + timedelta(seconds=_refresh_ttl_seconds()),
115	                ip=request.client.host if request.client else None,
116	                user_agent=request.headers.get("user-agent"),
117	            )
118	        )
119	        await session.commit()
120	    return body
121	
122	
123	async def _load_session(session: AsyncSession, sid: uuid.UUID) -> RefreshSession | None:
124	    result = await session.execute(select(RefreshSession).where(RefreshSession.id == sid))
125	    return result.scalar_one_or_none()
126	
127	
128	async def _revoke_family(session: AsyncSession, sid: uuid.UUID, now: datetime) -> None:
129	    await session.execute(
130	        update(RefreshSession).where(RefreshSession.id == sid).values(revoked_at=now)
131	    )
132	    await session.commit()
133	
134	
135	@router.post("/refresh", response_model=TokenResponse)
136	async def refresh(
137	    request: Request,
138	    response: Response,
139	    session: SessionDep,
140	) -> TokenResponse:
141	    token = request.cookies.get(_COOKIE_NAME)
142	    if not token:
143	        raise AuthError(message="Missing refresh token", code="auth.invalid_token")
144	
145	    claims = auth.decode_token(token, expected_typ="refresh")
146	    try:
147	        sid = uuid.UUID(claims["sid"])
148	        tenant_id = uuid.UUID(claims["tenant_id"])
149	        user_id = uuid.UUID(claims["sub"])
150	    except (KeyError, ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
151	        raise AuthError(message="Invalid refresh token", code="auth.invalid_token") from exc
152	
153	    # Refresh sets the tenancy ContextVar directly from the validated claim (D-007
154	    # item 1: refresh does NOT use system_context), so the session loads run scoped.
155	    current_tenant_id.set(tenant_id)
156	
157	    sess = await _load_session(session, sid)
158	    now = auth.now_utc()
159	    if sess is None or sess.revoked_at is not None or auth.as_utc(sess.expires_at) <= now:
160	        raise AuthError(message="Invalid refresh token", code="auth.invalid_token")
161	
162	    presented_hash = auth.sha256_hex(claims["jti"])
163	
164	    if presented_hash == sess.current_jti_hash:
165	        return await _rotate(session, sess, user_id, tenant_id, response, now)
166	
167	    within_grace = (
168	        sess.prev_jti_hash is not None
169	        and presented_hash == sess.prev_jti_hash
170	        and sess.rotated_at is not None
171	        and (now - auth.as_utc(sess.rotated_at)) < timedelta(seconds=_GRACE_SECONDS)
172	    )
173	    if within_grace:
174	        # Benign concurrent refresh (a second tab raced or a response was lost):
175	        # rotate again from the CURRENT chain rather than revoking the family.
176	        return await _rotate(session, sess, user_id, tenant_id, response, now)
177	
178	    # Any other mismatch is a replay of a stale token: kill the whole session family.
179	    await _revoke_family(session, sid, now)
180	    raise AuthError(message="Refresh token reuse detected", code="auth.invalid_token")
181	
182	
183	async def _rotate(
184	    session: AsyncSession,
185	    sess: RefreshSession,
186	    user_id: uuid.UUID,
187	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
188	    response: Response,
189	    now: datetime,
190	) -> TokenResponse:
191	    """Issue a new token pair and compare-and-swap the session's jti chain. The CAS
192	    WHERE clause makes a true race deterministic: the loser updates 0 rows and gets a
193	    401 (it will retry through the grace branch with the prev jti). token_version is
194	    re-read from the user row so a mid-session global revoke takes effect on refresh."""
195	    user = (
196	        await session.execute(select(User).where(User.id == user_id))
197	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
198	    if user is None or not user.is_active:
199	        raise AuthError(message="Invalid refresh token", code="auth.invalid_token")
200	
201	    sid = sess.id
202	    body, new_jti = _issue_tokens(response, user_id, tenant_id, sid, user.token_version, now)
203	    new_hash = auth.sha256_hex(new_jti)
204	    old_current = sess.current_jti_hash
205	
206	    result = await session.execute(
207	        update(RefreshSession)
208	        .where(RefreshSession.id == sid, RefreshSession.current_jti_hash == old_current)
209	        .values(
210	            prev_jti_hash=old_current,
211	            current_jti_hash=new_hash,
212	            rotated_at=now,
213	            last_used_at=now,
214	        )
215	    )
216	    if result.rowcount == 0:
217	        # Lost a true CAS race: another worker rotated first. Roll back and 401; the
218	        # client retries and lands in the grace branch on the next attempt.
219	        await session.rollback()
220	        raise AuthError(message="Concurrent refresh", code="auth.invalid_token")
221	    await session.commit()
222	    return body
223	
224	
225	@router.post("/logout", status_code=204)
226	async def logout(
227	    request: Request,
228	    response: Response,
229	    session: SessionDep,
230	) -> Response:
231	    # Best-effort revoke: even a malformed/expired cookie clears client state.
232	    token = request.cookies.get(_COOKIE_NAME)
233	    if token:
234	        try:
235	            claims = auth.decode_token(token, expected_typ="refresh")
236	            sid = uuid.UUID(claims["sid"])
237	            current_tenant_id.set(uuid.UUID(claims["tenant_id"]))
238	            await _revoke_family(session, sid, auth.now_utc())
239	        except (AuthError, KeyError, ValueError, TypeError):
240	            pass
241	    _clear_refresh_cookie(response)
242	    response.status_code = 204
243	    return response
244	
245	
246	@router.get("/me", response_model=MeResponse)
247	async def me(
248	    current: CurrentUserDep,
249	    session: SessionDep,
250	) -> MeResponse:
251	    # get_current_user already set the tenant context, so this select is scoped.
252	    user = (
253	        await session.execute(select(User).where(User.id == current.user_id))
254	    ).scalar_one()
255	    return MeResponse(
256	        id=user.id,
257	        tenant_id=user.tenant_id,
258	        email=user.email,
259	        full_name=user.full_name,
260	        permissions=sorted(current.permissions),
261	    )

1	"""audit
2	
3	Revision ID: 0005
4	Revises: 0004
5	Create Date: 2026-06-12
6	
7	core_audit_log (D-010): append-only audit trail. UuidPKMixin + TenantMixin (tenant_id of
8	the CHANGED row) + TimestampMixin (created_at = when written). Carries actor_user_id,
9	entity_table, entity_id (stringified PK), action (INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE), diff (JSON/JSONB),
10	request_id, request_ip. Two composite indexes lead with tenant_id so they are named
11	explicitly (the D-022 convention keys on column 0 and would collide).
12	
13	APPEND-ONLY is enforced at the DB by per-dialect triggers (D-022 trigger template): any
14	UPDATE or DELETE raises 'ATLAS_AUDIT_APPEND_ONLY', which core/exceptions translates to a
15	409 envelope. Trigger names are stable (trg_core_audit_log_no_update / _no_delete);
16	upgrade DROPs IF EXISTS then CREATEs; downgrade drops the triggers and the table.
17	
18	No batch-alter of a trigger-bearing table happens here; were one to, D-022 requires
19	re-executing this trigger DDL afterwards because SQLite copy-rebuild silently drops it.
20	"""
21	
22	import sqlalchemy as sa
23	from alembic import op
24	
25	from app.core.models import JSON_VARIANT
26	
27	# revision identifiers, used by Alembic.
28	revision: str = "0005"
29	down_revision: str | None = "0004"
30	branch_labels: str | None = None
31	depends_on: str | None = None
32	
33	_TABLE = "core_audit_log"
34	_TRG_NO_UPDATE = "trg_core_audit_log_no_update"
35	_TRG_NO_DELETE = "trg_core_audit_log_no_delete"
36	_GUARD_FN = "core_audit_log_append_only"
37	
38	# Postgres: one plpgsql function reused by both triggers; RAISE surfaces through asyncpg
39	# carrying the token. The function is created idempotently and dropped on downgrade.
40	_PG_FUNCTION = f"""
41	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION {_GUARD_FN}() RETURNS trigger AS $$
42	BEGIN
43	    RAISE EXCEPTION 'ATLAS_AUDIT_APPEND_ONLY';
44	END;
45	$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
46	"""
47	_PG_TRG_UPDATE = (
48	    f"CREATE TRIGGER {_TRG_NO_UPDATE} BEFORE UPDATE ON {_TABLE} "
49	    f"FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION {_GUARD_FN}();"
50	)
51	_PG_TRG_DELETE = (
52	    f"CREATE TRIGGER {_TRG_NO_DELETE} BEFORE DELETE ON {_TABLE} "
53	    f"FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION {_GUARD_FN}();"
54	)
55	
56	# SQLite: BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE triggers that RAISE(ABORT); the token surfaces as an
57	# IntegrityError carrying the message.
58	_SQLITE_TRG_UPDATE = (
59	    f"CREATE TRIGGER {_TRG_NO_UPDATE} BEFORE UPDATE ON {_TABLE} "
60	    f"BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'ATLAS_AUDIT_APPEND_ONLY'); END;"
61	)
62	_SQLITE_TRG_DELETE = (
63	    f"CREATE TRIGGER {_TRG_NO_DELETE} BEFORE DELETE ON {_TABLE} "
64	    f"BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'ATLAS_AUDIT_APPEND_ONLY'); END;"
65	)
66	
67	
68	def upgrade() -> None:
69	    op.create_table(
70	        _TABLE,
71	        sa.Column("id", sa.Uuid(), nullable=False),
72	        sa.Column("tenant_id", sa.Uuid(), nullable=False),
73	        sa.Column("actor_user_id", sa.Uuid(), nullable=True),
74	        sa.Column("entity_table", sa.String(length=100), nullable=False),
75	        sa.Column("entity_id", sa.String(length=100), nullable=False),
76	        sa.Column("action", sa.String(length=10), nullable=False),
77	        sa.Column("diff", JSON_VARIANT, nullable=False),
78	        sa.Column("request_id", sa.String(length=64), nullable=True),
79	        sa.Column("request_ip", sa.String(length=45), nullable=True),
80	        sa.Column(
81	            "created_at", sa.DateTime(timezone=True), server_default=sa.func.now(), nullable=False
82	        ),
83	        sa.Column(
84	            "updated_at", sa.DateTime(timezone=True), server_default=sa.func.now(), nullable=False
85	        ),
86	        sa.PrimaryKeyConstraint("id", name=op.f("pk_core_audit_log")),
87	    )
88	    op.create_index(op.f("ix_core_audit_log_tenant_id"), _TABLE, ["tenant_id"])
89	    op.create_index(
90	        "ix_core_audit_log_tenant_id_entity_table_entity_id",
91	        _TABLE,
92	        ["tenant_id", "entity_table", "entity_id"],
93	    )
94	    op.create_index("ix_core_audit_log_tenant_id_created_at", _TABLE, ["tenant_id", "created_at"])
95	
96	    op.execute(f"DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS {_TRG_NO_UPDATE}")
97	    op.execute(f"DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS {_TRG_NO_DELETE}")
98	    if op.get_bind().dialect.name == "postgresql":
99	        op.execute(_PG_FUNCTION)
100	        op.execute(_PG_TRG_UPDATE)
101	        op.execute(_PG_TRG_DELETE)
102	        # Defense in depth (D-010): the app role cannot mutate audit rows even if a
103	        # trigger were dropped. Scoped to the current role so it stays portable.
104	        op.execute(f"REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE ON {_TABLE} FROM CURRENT_USER")
105	    else:
106	        op.execute(_SQLITE_TRG_UPDATE)
107	        op.execute(_SQLITE_TRG_DELETE)
108	
109	
110	def downgrade() -> None:
111	    op.execute(f"DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS {_TRG_NO_UPDATE}")
112	    op.execute(f"DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS {_TRG_NO_DELETE}")
113	    if op.get_bind().dialect.name == "postgresql":
114	        op.execute(f"DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS {_GUARD_FN}()")
115	    op.drop_index("ix_core_audit_log_tenant_id_created_at", table_name=_TABLE)
116	    op.drop_index("ix_core_audit_log_tenant_id_entity_table_entity_id", table_name=_TABLE)
117	    op.drop_index(op.f("ix_core_audit_log_tenant_id"), table_name=_TABLE)
118	    op.drop_table(_TABLE)
